data.body_html:
Planning a hen party in Marbella? A yacht charter is the ultimate way to celebrate, but knowing exactly what you are paying for can be tricky. This marbella hen party yacht budget breakdown catering guide covers the two main package tiers, what is included, and how to stretch your budget without sacrificing the experience. All prices are in euros and include VAT, skipper, fuel, drinks, and snacks.

Tier A: Affordable Hen Party Charters (€749–€2,299)

Our Tier A boats are the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax). Both depart from Puerto Banús and come with a full drinks package: water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava, plus light snacks. The 2-hour sunset cruise at €749 works out at roughly €68 per person for a group of 11. For a full day (8 hours) at €2,299, that is about €209 per person. This tier is ideal for smaller groups who want a private, stylish experience without the luxury price tag.

Tier B: Premium Hen Party Charters with Jet Ski (from €4,719)

For larger groups or those wanting more space, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) and its grey variant are available from €4,719 for a minimum 4 hours. This includes a free jet ski, which is a huge hit for hen parties. With 12 guests, that’s €393 per person for 4 hours. The boat features a large sundeck, saloon, and plenty of photo opportunities. All standard inclusions apply: skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance. No hidden fees.

What the Standard Catering Package Includes

Every charter in our fleet includes the same base catering package: unlimited water, soft drinks (Coke, Sprite, tonic), beer (local lager), white wine, and cava. Light snacks such as crisps, nuts, and olives are provided. This is sufficient for most 2-4 hour trips. For longer charters, you may want to upgrade. The drinks are served in disposable cups, and you are welcome to bring your own cooler if you prefer specific brands.

Upgrading Your Catering: Options and Costs

If you want a more elaborate spread, we can arrange catering upgrades on request. Options include premium charcuterie boards, fresh seafood platters (prawns, oysters), sushi, or a full paella buffet. Prices vary depending on the menu and number of guests. For example, a deluxe seafood platter for 12 people typically costs €200–€350 extra. Champagne upgrades (a bottle of Moët or Veuve Clicquot) start at €80 per bottle. Contact us via WhatsApp to discuss your preferences and get a quote.

Budget Tips for a Hen Party Yacht Charter

  • Book a 4-hour slot – It’s the sweet spot between cost and experience. You get time to cruise the coast, swim, and enjoy drinks without fatigue.
  • Split costs evenly – Use a group payment app. With 10 guests on a Tier A boat, a 4-hour charter (€1,299) costs €130 per person.
  • Choose Tier A for smaller groups – The Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 are perfect for 8-11 hens. You save money and still get a luxury feel.
  • Go for a morning charter – Morning slots (10:00–14:00) are often cheaper than afternoon or sunset, and the sea is calmer.
  • Bring your own playlist – All boats have Bluetooth speakers. Create a hen party playlist beforehand to save time.

Comparing Tier A vs Tier B: Which Is Right for Your Hen Party?

Hidden Costs to Watch Out For

Our prices are all-inclusive of VAT (21%), skipper, fuel, insurance, and the standard catering. However, there are a few extras you might want to budget for: a tip for the skipper (10–15% is customary), catering upgrades, and any private transfers to Puerto Banús. If you want a photographer or videographer onboard, that can be arranged separately (approx. €200–€400 for 2 hours). Always confirm the final total before booking.

How to Book Your Hen Party Yacht Charter

Booking is straightforward. Choose your preferred boat from our fleet list, check availability, and pay a deposit (usually 30–50%). The balance is due 30 days before departure. We recommend booking at least 2–4 weeks in advance for summer weekends. For last-minute inquiries, contact us via WhatsApp and we will do our best to accommodate. All charters depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella’s iconic marina.
